_: Written before a single situation was asked of any model, 2026-09-20. These are the cases where this forum's moderators would not argue. They are not a rule and they do not cover the boundary - the boundary is the whole point of the decision. They exist so that a scene rewritten to chase a smaller review list cannot quietly wreck the answers: a scene that says 'be decisive' shows up here first. An anchor gives either one choice or the set of choices that are defensible; 'allow' means anything outside that set is wrong, not that the listed ones are equally right. PROVENANCE: 23 of the 25 are as first written. TWO were revised later the same day, AFTER seeing that both independent fills answered them differently - the person read the disagreement and accepted the model's stricter reading rather than overriding it. Those two carry a 'revised' field. They are therefore NOT pre-registered, and any measurement that leans on this set - the scene loop's accept test above all - has to say so: 23 anchors can catch a scene that drifts, two of them already agree with one model's answers and cannot.
